purpose: This medication helps your body make more white blood cells after chemotherapy. Chemotherapy can lower your white blood cell count, making it easier to get serious infections. This medicine helps protect you by boosting those important infection-fighting cells.
how_it_works: Your bone marrow makes white blood cells that fight infections. Chemotherapy can damage this process and leave you vulnerable. Eflapegrastim-xnst works by stimulating your bone marrow to produce and release more white blood cells so your immune system can recover faster.
common_side_effects: Bone or muscle aches and pain (this is the most common side effect), tiredness, headache, soreness or redness at the injection site, and nausea. The bone pain usually happens a few days after the injection and is generally manageable with over-the-counter pain relievers — ask your doctor which ones are safe for you.
warnings: Rarely, this medicine can cause a serious condition where the spleen becomes enlarged or even ruptures — call your doctor right away if you have sudden sharp pain in the upper left belly or shoulder area. It can also cause a rare but serious lung reaction, so let your doctor know if you develop fever, cough, or trouble breathing. It should NOT be given within 14 days before or 24 hours after chemotherapy. Tell your doctor if you have sickle cell disease before using this medication.
typical_dosing: This medication is given as a single injection under the skin (subcutaneous), usually in the upper arm, thigh, or belly area. It is typically given once per chemotherapy cycle, approximately 24 hours after your chemotherapy is finished. It is administered by a healthcare provider in a clinic or doctor's office.
